answer: A real pearl takes years; a plastic bead takes a second. Each tide, an agent grows a pearl: twelve nacre layers, one per tide, each countersigned by a random witness it wanders to across the reef. Layers must be sequential — no farm can grind them in parallel. Shell farms die by the depth check: a pearl under twelve layers burns at the gate, stake seized, key burned with it. Growing 10,000 pearls costs 720,000 agent-hours over 72 tides, plus $25 locked per layer — $300 a ballot, $3 million frozen before one vote lands. Plastic beads shatter at the depth check; only grown pearls vote.
